# window


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

This module is the part of kavacha that runs inside the finished app. It
opens a native window that shows a web app served from a loopback
address, one on the same machine such as 127.0.0.1, and gives that
window what people expect of a desktop app: a menu bar, a Dock menu of
recent folders, a window that hides instead of quitting when it is
closed, and a response when a folder is dropped on the app’s icon.
pywebview draws the window, and most of the platform-specific parts are
for macOS.

The application that uses kavacha is called the host here. It supplies
its name, its menus and the callbacks that do its own work, such as
opening a folder.
[`run_shell`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#run_shell),
near the end, is the function a host calls. Everything above it is a
piece
[`run_shell`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#run_shell)
is built from.

### use_app

``` python
def use_app(
    name, cfg:NoneType=None, env_prefix:str='KAVACHA_'
):
```

*Set the app name, the config and storage folders, and the environment
variable prefix kavacha uses.*

A few things are named after the app: the folder where the window keeps
its settings and browser storage, the title on the holding page, and the
prefix of the environment variables kavacha reads. `APP_NAME` is that
name. It is read from `$KAVACHA_APP_NAME` when the module is imported
and defaults to `app`. `CFG` is the settings folder, from `$KAVACHA_CFG`
or else the XDG config folder named after the app, such as
`~/.config/app`.

A host should call
[`use_app`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#use_app)
once, before it opens a window, with its own name. It sets `APP_NAME`,
`CFG`, `STORAGE` and the environment variable prefix together. After
`use_app('leela', env_prefix='LEELA_')`, for example, the window size
comes from `$LEELA_WINDOW_SIZE` instead of `$KAVACHA_WINDOW_SIZE`, and
the settings folder from `$LEELA_CFG`. None of this creates anything on
disk.

[`errstr`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#errstr)
formats an exception as its type and its message. Every warning this
module prints uses it. The type is kept because many messages say little
on their own: a `KeyError` carries only the missing key.


`DEFAULT_SIZE` is a new window’s size when nothing else is asked for.
`MIN_SIZE` is the smallest size the user can drag a window to, and the
smallest
[`window_size`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#window_size)
accepts. `STORAGE` is the folder inside `CFG` where the web view keeps
cookies and local storage between runs. `EAGER_CDP` holds the name of
the environment variable
[`warm_cdp`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#warm_cdp)
reads, described below. `BACKENDS` is the same table as in
`kavacha.probe`.

``` python
DEFAULT_SIZE, MIN_SIZE, str(STORAGE).replace(str(CFG), '/cfg')
```

### ShellApi

``` python
def ShellApi(
    *args, **kwargs
):
```

*What the page may ask the native window for, as
`window.pywebview.api.*`.*

The page in the window sometimes needs the operating system, for example
to show the native folder chooser. pywebview allows this through a
JavaScript API: the methods of a Python object become functions the page
calls as `window.pywebview.api.<method>()`.
[`ShellApi`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#shellapi)
is that object.

`pick_folder` shows the platform’s folder chooser and returns the chosen
path, or `None` if the user cancels. `pick_path` does the same with a
chooser that takes a file or a folder, as File \> Open does in a Mac
app. `open_folder` and `recent` pass the request to the host’s
`on_open_folder` and `on_recent` callbacks, which
[`run_shell`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#run_shell)
sets. Without a callback, `open_folder` returns `False` and `recent`
returns an empty list. `open_path` takes either kind: a folder goes the
way of `open_folder`, and a file goes to `on_open_file`, the callback a
file opened from Finder reaches. A host that must tell a request from
the page apart from a Finder or Dock open sets `on_page_folder`:
`open_folder` then calls it in place of `on_open_folder`. `on_picked`
gets each folder the person chooses in `pick_folder` or `pick_path`,
before the page sees it, so the host can trust that one path. It is not
called for a file or when the person cancels. pywebview calls these
methods on its own worker threads, so the callbacks must be safe to call
from any thread. `dropped` is for files dropped on the window, described
with
[`arm_drops`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#arm_drops)
below. The page cannot call the `on_` callbacks themselves: pywebview
offers the page every function an object lists, so
[`ShellApi`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#shellapi)
lists none of them.

`set_background` is for a page with themes. It takes the page’s
background as `#rrggbb` and paints every open window’s native background
with it, which is what shows while the window opens or grows faster than
the page redraws. It also keeps the colour in `background`, so a window
opened later starts on it. The colour is per app, not per window:
pywebview does not say which window called. Anything that is not
`#rrggbb` returns `False` and changes nothing.

``` python
api = ShellApi()
opened = []
api.on_open_folder = opened.append
api.open_folder('/proj/demo'), api.open_folder(''), opened
```

    (True, False, ['/proj/demo'])

A page request goes to `on_page_folder` when the host sets it. Finder
and the Dock still use `on_open_folder`.

``` python
two, page = ShellApi(), []
two.on_open_folder, two.on_page_folder = opened.append, page.append
two.open_folder('/proj/two')
test_eq(page, ['/proj/two'])
test_eq(opened, ['/proj/demo'])
```

`on_picked` gets the folder the person chose, and is not called on a
cancel. A fake `webview` module stands in for the real chooser.

``` python
import sys, tempfile, types
from unittest.mock import patch
```

``` python
def fake_webview(answer): return types.SimpleNamespace(FileDialog=types.SimpleNamespace(FOLDER=20), active_window=lambda: types.SimpleNamespace(create_file_dialog=lambda kind: answer))
picked = []
two.on_picked = picked.append
with patch.dict(sys.modules, webview=fake_webview(['/proj/chosen'])): test_eq(two.pick_folder(), '/proj/chosen')
with patch.dict(sys.modules, webview=fake_webview(None)): test_eq(two.pick_folder(), None)
test_eq(picked, ['/proj/chosen'])
```

### choose_path

``` python
def choose_path(
    window
):
```

*Paths from a chooser that takes one file or one folder: `NSOpenPanel`
on macOS, pywebview’s file dialog elsewhere.*

pywebview’s own dialog chooses files or folders, never both, so
[`choose_path`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#choose_path)
builds the macOS panel itself, on the main thread where AppKit wants it,
and waits for the answer. Off macOS it shows the file dialog, which
chooses files only. `pick_path` calls `on_picked` only when the choice
is a folder, and `open_path` sends it on by its kind. A stand-in
[`choose_path`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#choose_path)
shows both.

``` python
_d2 = tempfile.mkdtemp(); _f2 = os.path.join(_d2, 'a.png'); open(_f2, 'w').close()
three, files, folders, picked = ShellApi(), [], [], []
three.on_open_file, three.on_page_folder, three.on_picked = files.append, folders.append, picked.append
for got in ([_f2], [_d2], [], None):
    with patch.dict(sys.modules, webview=fake_webview(None)), patch(f'{__name__}.choose_path', lambda w, got=got: got):
        p = three.pick_path()
        if p: three.open_path(p)
test_eq((files, folders, picked), ([_f2], [_d2], [_d2]))
test_eq((three.open_path(''), ShellApi().open_path(_f2)), (False, False))
test_eq([n for n in dir(three) if n.startswith('on_')], [])
assert {'open_path', 'pick_path', 'dropped'} <= set(dir(three))
```

*Wait until `url` gives any HTTP response or `timeout` seconds pass, and

[`wait_for_http`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/probe.html#wait_for_http)
waits until the server at `url` answers or `timeout` seconds pass, and
returns whether it answered. Unlike the version in `kavacha.probe`, any
HTTP response counts, including an error such as 404, because a server
that sends an error page has started. Only a failed connection means it
is not ready. The example asks for a page that does not exist and still
gets `True`.


### warm_cdp

``` python
def warm_cdp(
    port:NoneType=None, profile:NoneType=None
):
```

*Start the CDP Chrome at launch, but only when the `EAGER_CDP`
environment variable is 1, true or yes.*

Some hosts show web pages inside the app through a separate Chrome that
they control over the Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP), using fossick.
[`start_cdp`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#start_cdp)
starts that Chrome on `port` in a background thread and returns the
thread. If a Chrome is already listening on `port`, it does nothing. If
fossick is not installed or Chrome fails to start, it prints a message
and the app carries on without it. Pass `wait=True` to wait for the
start, for up to `timeout` seconds or 30 by default. `profile` is the
Chrome user data folder.

[`cdp_target`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#cdp_target)
picks the port and the profile. A visible Chrome uses `port`, or
`CDP_PORT` (9223), and `profile`, or fastcdp’s own profile. A headless
Chrome uses `HEADLESS_PORT` (9224) and `HEADLESS_PROFILE`. It never uses
port 9223 or fastcdp’s profile, because those belong to the visible CDP
Chrome. A headless Chrome on that port and profile takes over the
visible Chrome: a click on its app then opens nothing. fossick starts
Chrome through fastcdp’s `chrome_bin`, so the `FASTCDP_CHROME`
environment variable chooses the browser.

Starting Chrome takes time and memory, so a host normally starts it the
first time it is needed.
[`warm_cdp`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#warm_cdp)
starts it at launch instead, but only when the environment variable
named in `EAGER_CDP`, `KAVACHA_CDP_EAGER` unless
[`use_app`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#use_app)
changed the prefix, is `1`, `true` or `yes` in lower case. Otherwise it
returns `None`.

### is_light

``` python
def is_light(
    colour
):
```

*Whether `#rrggbb` is a light colour, so dark ink reads on it.*

A window opens at once, but its server may take a few seconds to start.
Until it does, the window shows a holding page made by
[`splash`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#splash):
the app’s name in large type and a short note under it, on the window’s
background, which is dark unless the host gives another. On a light
background the text is dark. The page is self-contained and loads
nothing from the network. If the server never answers, the window shows
the same page with the note replaced, in red, by the address that did
not answer.
[`_unreachable`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#_unreachable)
makes that version, and the example shows its last line.

``` python
_unreachable('http://127.0.0.1:8000/').splitlines()[-1]
```

    '<div><b>app</b><i style="color:#e06c75">the workspace at http://127.0.0.1:8000/ did not answer</i></div>'

### dock_menu

``` python
def dock_menu(
    on_folder, recent:NoneType=None
):
```

*The Dock’s own menu: the folders last open, newest first. `recent` is
the host’s list of paths.*

On macOS, right-clicking an app’s Dock icon shows a menu.
[`dock_menu`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#dock_menu)
fills it with the folders the user opened most recently, newest first,
up to `DOCK_RECENT` of them. Each row shows the folder’s name, with the
full path as its tooltip, and choosing one calls `on_folder` with the
path. `recent` is the host’s list of paths, already in order. With no
recent folders the menu holds a single disabled row that says so. The
function needs AppKit, so there is no example here.

### dock_delegates

``` python
def dock_delegates():
```

*The two delegate subclasses. Built once: an Objective-C class name is
global to the runtime.*

Most macOS apps keep running when their last window is closed, and
clicking the Dock icon brings the window back. kavacha does the same.
Closing a window hides it, and clicking the Dock icon shows the window
that was hidden most recently. Quitting with Cmd+Q still ends the app,
after running
[`quit_cleanly`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#quit_cleanly).
This works by replacing pywebview’s window and app delegates, the
objects AppKit asks how to respond to events such as a window closing;
[`dock_delegates`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#dock_delegates)
builds the two replacement classes once, and
[`keep_running_in_dock`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#keep_running_in_dock),
below, installs them. The hidden windows wait in `hidden_windows`, the
most recently hidden last.

### quit_cleanly

``` python
def quit_cleanly(
    timeout:int=15, run_exit:NoneType=None, grace:float=1.0
):
```

*Stop this process’s multiprocessing children, then run its atexit
handlers, which a Cocoa quit’s C `exit()` skips.*

When a Cocoa app quits, it ends the process with C’s `exit()`, which
skips Python’s atexit handlers, and worker processes can outlive it. A
worker pool started by forking, as `fastcore.parallel` does on macOS,
keeps pipes open that hold its children alive.
[`quit_cleanly`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#quit_cleanly)
terminates each child process of this one, kills any still running after
one shared `grace` of a second, then runs the atexit handlers on a
thread and waits at most `timeout` seconds for them. It reaps once more
afterwards, for a pool a still-running thread started meanwhile, and
returns the number of children it stopped. It sets `quitting` first, so
a host’s background job can tell being reaped from failing. `run_exit`
replaces the atexit handlers, which is how the test below checks it
without exiting.

[`quit_on_sigterm`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#quit_on_sigterm)
makes a SIGTERM, the signal `kill` sends by default, quit the app the
way Cmd+Q does, so that the same clean-up runs. It works on macOS only,
must be called on the main thread, and is called by
[`run_shell`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#run_shell).
A forked child gets the default SIGTERM back and lets go of the wakeup
socket, and a multiprocessing child exits once its parent is gone, so a
Force Quit or a crash leaves no idle worker behind. Once a quit begins,
a second SIGTERM kills.

``` python
import multiprocessing as mp, subprocess, tempfile
```

``` python
kid = mp.get_context('fork').Process(target=time.sleep, args=(60,)); kid.start()
ran = []
test_eq(quit_cleanly(run_exit=lambda: ran.append(1)), 1)
test_eq((kid.is_alive(), ran), (False, [1]))
t0 = time.time(); quit_cleanly(timeout=.3, run_exit=lambda: time.sleep(30))
assert time.time() - t0 < 5, 'a hung handler does not hold the quit'
```

``` python
_fork_probe = r'''
import os, signal, sys, time, multiprocessing as mp
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
from kavacha.window import quit_on_sigterm, quit_cleanly
def ignore(): signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, signal.SIG_IGN); time.sleep(60)
def nested(path):
    ex = ProcessPoolExecutor(2, mp_context=mp.get_context('fork')); list(ex.map(abs, range(4)))
    open(path, 'w').write(' '.join(str(p.pid) for p in mp.active_children())); time.sleep(60)
def alive(pid):
    try: os.kill(pid, 0); return True
    except OSError: return False
if __name__ == '__main__':
    r, w = quit_on_sigterm(); r.setblocking(False)
    fork = mp.get_context('fork')
    kid = fork.Process(target=time.sleep, args=(60,)); kid.start(); time.sleep(.3)
    kid.terminate(); kid.join(5)
    assert kid.exitcode == -signal.SIGTERM, kid.exitcode
    try: assert not r.recv(64), "a child's SIGTERM reached the parent's wakeup socket"
    except BlockingIOError: pass
    ex = ProcessPoolExecutor(4, mp_context=fork); list(ex.map(abs, range(8)))
    pool = [p.pid for p in mp.active_children()]
    stubborn = [fork.Process(target=ignore) for _ in range(4)]
    for p in stubborn: p.start()
    time.sleep(.5); t0 = time.time()
    assert quit_cleanly(run_exit=lambda: None, grace=.5) == 8
    assert time.time() - t0 < 4, f'{time.time()-t0:.1f}s: one shared grace, not one per child'
    assert not [p for p in pool if alive(p)], 'pool workers outlived quit_cleanly'
    assert signal.getsignal(signal.SIGTERM) == signal.SIG_DFL, 'a second SIGTERM must kill a hung quit'
    mid = fork.Process(target=nested, args=(sys.argv[1],)); mid.start()
    while not os.path.exists(sys.argv[1]) or not open(sys.argv[1]).read(): time.sleep(.1)
    grand = [int(x) for x in open(sys.argv[1]).read().split()]
    os.kill(mid.pid, signal.SIGKILL); mid.join()
    end = time.time() + 5
    while [g for g in grand if alive(g)] and time.time() < end: time.sleep(.2)
    assert not [g for g in grand if alive(g)], 'workers outlived a parent that was SIGKILLed'
    print('ok')
'''
if sys.platform == 'darwin':
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '-c', _fork_probe, f'{d}/grand'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
    assert r.stdout.strip() == 'ok', r.stdout + r.stderr
```


*Turn off the system’s autocorrect for this app. True when it took.*

macOS corrects text as you type: it turns straight quotes into curly
ones, a pair of hyphens into a dash, and fixes spelling. In a code
editor that corrupts what you type.
[`quiet_text_substitution`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#quiet_text_substitution)
turns these corrections off for this app only, by setting the keys in
`NO_SUBSTITUTION` in the app’s user defaults, and returns whether that
worked. On other platforms it does nothing and returns `False`.

``` python
    on_folder:NoneType=None, recent:NoneType=None
):
```

*Hide the last window rather than quit, and fill the Dock menu. Reopen
shows one window. Cmd+Q quits.*

[`keep_running_in_dock`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#keep_running_in_dock)
installs the hide-on-close behaviour and the Dock menu described above.
Call it before the first window is created, because pywebview uses the
delegate classes it has at that moment. `on_folder` is called with a
path chosen from the Dock menu, and `recent` returns the host’s recent
folders. It returns `True` when the delegates were installed, or prints
why and returns `False` if pywebview’s Cocoa platform cannot be loaded.

`WINDOW_KW` holds the settings every window is created with: the minimum
size, which is `MIN_SIZE`, the dark background shown while a page loads,
text selection, zoom, and no dragging of the window by its content. The
title and the size are left out because they are the only things that
differ from one window to the next. A window opened at launch and one
opened an hour later for another folder therefore behave the same.

### make_window

``` python
def make_window(
    title:NoneType=None, size:NoneType=None, background:NoneType=None
):
```

*A window on the splash, waiting for a URL, on
`window_background(background)`.*

[`make_window`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#make_window)
creates a window showing the splash page, titled `title` (the app’s name
by default) and sized `size` (from
[`window_size`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#window_size)
by default). It does not load a URL;
[`open_window`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#open_window)
and
[`run_shell`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#run_shell)
do that once the server answers. It also creates the `STORAGE` folder if
needed. The window and its splash take `window_background(background)`,
so with no `background` a window opens on the colour the page last set.
On macOS each page the window loads gets
[`arm_drops`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#arm_drops),
so a file dropped on it opens.

## A unified title bar

A host whose page draws its own top row can merge that row with the
window’s title bar. The host sets `shell_api().unified = True` before it
opens windows, and each platform then does what is native to it:

- On macOS the page lies under a transparent title bar with no title. An
  empty unified toolbar makes the bar 52 points high, so the traffic
  lights sit centred in the page’s top row. The page leaves about 80
  pixels free at its left for them. The title is still set, so the
  Window menu, Mission Control and tools that read the title still have
  it.
- On Windows the native caption stays, with its minimise, maximise and
  close buttons, snap layouts and keyboard behaviour.
  [`tint_caption`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#tint_caption)
  paints it in the page’s background, with dark mode on a dark one, so
  the caption and the page’s top row read as one bar. Windows 11 takes
  the caption colours; Windows 10 takes only dark mode.
- Elsewhere nothing changes.

The page learns the mode two ways:
[`with_titlebar`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#with_titlebar)
puts it on the first URL as `titlebar=<mode>`, so the page can lay out
its first paint, and
[`ShellApi.titlebar`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#shellapi.titlebar)
answers it once pywebview’s bridge is up. The page marks the row that
drags the window with pywebview’s `pywebview-drag-region` class. WebKit
ignores `-webkit-app-region`, so pywebview’s own drag code moves the
window, and only a press on the marked element itself starts a drag.

### off_main_thread

``` python
def off_main_thread(
    fn, name:str='kavacha-shell'
):
```

*Run `fn(arg)` on a thread of its own; `create_window` builds nothing on
the main thread.*

Native events, such as a click in the Dock menu or a folder dropped on
the app’s icon, arrive on the main thread, inside the GUI loop, and
pywebview cannot build a window from there.
[`off_main_thread`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#off_main_thread)
wraps `fn` so that each call runs on a new daemon thread named `name`
instead. The example records the name of the thread its callback ran on.

``` python
seen, done = [], Event()
go = off_main_thread(lambda p: (seen.append((p, threading.current_thread().name)), done.set()))
go('/proj/demo'); done.wait(5)
seen
```

    [('/proj/demo', 'kavacha-shell')]

### bring_forward

``` python
def bring_forward():
```

*Activate the app, and drop the hidden-window entries whose window is on
screen again. macOS only.*

[`open_window`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#open_window)
opens a window on `url` while the app is running, for example when the
user opens another folder. `key` identifies the window, such as the
folder’s path. If a window with that key is already open,
[`open_window`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#open_window)
shows it, even if it was hidden to the Dock, instead of opening a second
one. Either way it activates the app with
[`bring_forward`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#bring_forward),
so a window opened from Finder is not left behind other apps. The
windows that have a key are kept in the dictionary `keyed_windows`,
which
[`run_shell`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#run_shell)
also fills. Otherwise it creates a window, shows the splash, waits up to
`url_wait` seconds for the server and loads the page, or shows the
unreachable page if the server never answers. It blocks while it waits,
so call it from a thread made by
[`off_main_thread`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#off_main_thread).

The example uses stand-in windows. The first is brought to the front.
The second fails to come to the front, so
[`open_window`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#open_window)
prints why and returns it as it is.

``` python
keyed_windows['demo'], keyed_windows['gone'] = _Win(), _Win(fail=True)
u = 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/'
open_window(u, 'Demo', key='demo').calls, open_window(u, 'Notes', key='gone').calls
```

### unify_nswindow

``` python
def unify_nswindow(
    nsw, toolbar:NoneType=None
):
```

*Lay `nsw`’s content under a transparent title bar with no title, 52
points high so the traffic lights centre in the page’s top row.*

[`unified_titlebar`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#unified_titlebar)
is what
[`make_window`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#make_window)
runs before a unified window is shown. It finds pywebview’s own window
object, the `NSWindow` on macOS or the WinForms form on Windows, and
calls
[`unify_nswindow`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#unify_nswindow)
or
[`tint_caption`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#tint_caption)
on it. A Windows window keeps its handle as `window.hwnd`, so
[`paint_background`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#paint_background)
tints the caption again each time the page changes its theme. A failure
prints why and leaves the window as it was.

The examples use stand-in windows, so no real window opens. The Mac
stand-in records the calls AppKit would get; the Windows one records the
DWM attributes.

``` python
class _NSWindow:
    "Stands in for an NSWindow: it records what `unify_nswindow` sets."
    def __init__(self): self.mask, self.set = 15, {}
    def styleMask(self): return self.mask
    def setStyleMask_(self, m): self.mask = m
    def setTitlebarAppearsTransparent_(self, v): self.set['transparent'] = v
    def setTitleVisibility_(self, v): self.set['title'] = v
    def setToolbar_(self, t): self.set['toolbar'] = t
    def respondsToSelector_(self, s): return s == 'setToolbarStyle:'
    def setToolbarStyle_(self, v): self.set['style'] = v
class _Toolbar:
    def setShowsBaselineSeparator_(self, v): self.separator = v
class _PyWin: uid = 'w1'
nsw = _NSWindow()
unify_nswindow(nsw, _Toolbar()), nsw.mask, nsw.set['title']
```

### run_shell

``` python
def run_shell(
    urls, titles:tuple=(), url_wait:int=90, gui:NoneType=None, icon:NoneType=None, size:NoneType=None,
    on_ready:NoneType=None, on_open_folder:NoneType=None, keys:tuple=(), bar:tuple=(), lookup:NoneType=None,
    on_action:NoneType=None, on_recent:NoneType=None, background:NoneType=None, on_open_file:NoneType=None
):
```

*Open one native window per workspace URL and block until they close.*

[`run_shell`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#run_shell)
is the entry point. It opens one window per URL in the list `urls`,
titled with the matching entry of `titles`, and runs the GUI loop until
the app quits. Call it on the main thread, after starting the servers on
another thread or in another process. Each window shows the splash until
its server answers, for up to `url_wait` seconds. It raises a
`RuntimeError` if no window can be opened here and a `ValueError` if
`urls` is empty.

The other arguments are optional:

- `size` is a `(width, height)` tuple for every window; without it
  [`window_size`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#window_size)
  decides.
- `gui` overrides the pywebview GUI that
  [`shell_ready`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/probe.html#shell_ready)
  picks, and `icon` is the window icon.
- `on_ready` is called once every window has loaded its page.
- `on_open_folder` and `on_recent` are the host’s callbacks for opening
  a folder and for listing recent ones. They serve
  [`ShellApi`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#shellapi),
  the Dock menu and folders dropped on the app’s icon.
- `on_open_file` is called with the path of each file the user opens
  with the app from Finder, by double-click or Open With, whether the
  app is running or being launched by it.
- `keys` gives each window a key, so that
  [`open_window`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#open_window)
  can find it later.
- `background` is the colour every window opens on, as
  [`window_background`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#window_background)
  reads it: a host with themes passes its page background, so the window
  does not flash another colour before the page paints.
- `bar`, `lookup` and `on_action` describe the menu bar, as explained
  below.

On macOS it also turns off text substitution, keeps the app in the Dock
when its last window closes, and makes SIGTERM quit cleanly. Setting the
environment variable `<prefix>WEBVIEW_DEBUG` turns on pywebview’s debug
mode.

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### menus

``` python
def menus(
```

*Build the macOS menu bar, or return an empty list.*

[`menus`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#menus)
builds the macOS menu bar from the host’s table `bar` with
[`menu_bar`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#menu_bar)
and
[`install_menu_patch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#install_menu_patch),
both below, and turns off pywebview’s default menus. `lookup` and
`on_action` are explained with
[`menu_chord`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#menu_chord)
and
[`menu_bar`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#menu_bar),
and [`run`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/build.html#run) is the
function [`Js`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#js)
rows use,
[`eval_js`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#eval_js)
by default. On other platforms, or if anything fails, it returns an
empty list and the window has no menu bar.

A file or folder opened with the app reaches it in up to two ways: the
delegate’s `application:openFiles:`, and the raw `odoc` handler below.
[`open_paths`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#open_paths)
is where both end. It calls `on_folder` with each folder in `paths` and
`on_file` with each file, and returns `False` if some path had no
callback for its kind, which is how the delegate tells Finder the open
failed. A path is delivered once within `OPEN_TTL` seconds, so a single
open that both routes see does not open two windows.

### take_dropped

``` python
def take_dropped(
    names
):
```

*The full paths pywebview kept for the dropped files `names`, in order.
It forgets the rest, so a later drop never gets a stale path.*

A file or folder dragged from Finder onto the window, rather than onto
the app’s icon, is a drop in the web page. The page learns only the
file’s name, never its location. pywebview’s macOS view reads the full
paths from the drag and keeps them, but only while some drop listener is
registered, and
[`arm_drops`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#arm_drops)
makes sure one is counted.
[`make_window`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#make_window)
calls
[`arm_drops`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#arm_drops)
on every page load, and it adds `DROP_JS` to the page.

`DROP_JS` lets a file drag land anywhere, and it leaves every drop the
page handles itself to the page: a page handler that calls
`preventDefault` or `stopPropagation` keeps the drop, as an editor that
takes a file’s text does. When the drop is over, the script calls
`dropped` with the files’ names and whether the drop was left to the
window.
[`take_dropped`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#take_dropped)
exchanges the names for the paths pywebview kept, and forgets the rest.
`dropped` then opens the paths through
[`open_paths`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#open_paths),
with the same callbacks as a Finder open. A page script that calls
`dropped` gets nothing that was not dropped from outside, because
pywebview keeps no path for a drag that starts in the page, and each
page load forgets the paths of a drop that never reached `dropped`.

``` python
_dnd = types.SimpleNamespace(_dnd_state={'num_listeners': 0, 'paths': []})
_api4, _got4 = ShellApi(), []
_api4.on_open_folder, _api4.on_open_file = _rec('dir'), _rec('file')
_got.clear(); _seen.clear()
with patch.dict(sys.modules, {'webview.dom': _dnd}):
    _dnd._dnd_state['paths'] += [('x.md', str(_f)), (_d.name, str(_d)), ('old.png', '/gone/old.png')]
    test_eq(_api4.dropped(['x.md', _d.name]), [str(_f), str(_d)])
    test_eq(_got, [('file', str(_f)), ('dir', str(_d))])
    test_eq(_dnd._dnd_state['paths'], [])
    _dnd._dnd_state['paths'].append(('x.md', str(_f))); _seen.clear()
    test_eq(_api4.dropped(['x.md'], False), [])
    test_eq((len(_got), _dnd._dnd_state['paths']), (2, []))
    test_eq(_api4.dropped(['x.md']), [])
    _dnd._dnd_state['paths'] += [('x.md', '/a/x.md'), ('x.md', '/b/x.md'), ('cafe\u0301.md', '/c/caf.md')]
    test_eq(take_dropped(['x.md', 'x.md', 'caf\u00e9.md']), ['/a/x.md', '/b/x.md', '/c/caf.md'])
    _dnd._dnd_state['paths'].append(('x.md', str(_f)))
    w = types.SimpleNamespace(js=[], run_js=lambda s: w.js.append(s))
    arm_drops(w)
    test_eq((_dnd._dnd_state['num_listeners'], _dnd._dnd_state['paths'], w.js), (1, [], [DROP_JS]))
```

### watch_open_events

``` python
def watch_open_events(
    on_folder:NoneType=None, on_file:NoneType=None
):
```

*Answer the `odoc` Apple Event Finder sends a running app. macOS only,
best-effort.*

When the user drops a folder on the app’s Dock icon, or opens a folder
with the app from Finder, macOS sends the running app an “open
documents” Apple Event, `odoc`.
[`watch_open_events`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#watch_open_events)
registers a handler for it that hands the paths in the event to
[`open_paths`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#open_paths),
which calls `on_folder` for each folder and `on_file` for each file.
[`run_shell`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#run_shell)
registers it with the host’s callbacks, already wrapped by
[`off_main_thread`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#off_main_thread).
The app delegate receives the same opens through
`application:openFiles:`, and
[`open_paths`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#open_paths)
keeps a path that arrives both ways from being delivered twice. It
returns the handler, or `None` on other platforms or if registration
fails.

AppKit can only call methods on Objective-C objects, so the Dock menu
rows and the Apple Event handler each need a small `NSObject` subclass
that passes the call on to a Python function: `RecentTarget` for a Dock
menu row and `OpenHandler` for the event. Where pyobjc is not installed,
both classes are `None`, and the functions that use them only run on
macOS.

A menu bar shows keyboard shortcuts next to its items, and pressing one
runs the item even while the web page has focus. kavacha writes a
shortcut as a chord, such as `mod+s`: modifier names joined by `+`, then
a key, where `mod` means Cmd on a Mac. AppKit wants the same shortcut as
a key equivalent, which is a single character, plus a modifier mask, a
number with one bit per modifier key. `CMD`, `CTRL`, `ALT` and `SHIFT`
are those bits, defined here so that chords can be parsed and tested on
any platform.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/kavacha/blob/main/kavacha/window.py#L801"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### mac_key

``` python
def mac_key(
    chord
):
```

*`(keyEquivalent, modifierMask)` for one chord, or None when AppKit
cannot spell it.*

[`mac_key`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#mac_key)
converts one chord to a `(key, mask)` pair. It accepts the modifiers
`mod`, `cmd`, `ctrl`, `alt`, `opt` and `shift`, an upper-case letter as
shorthand for shift and that letter, and named keys such as `up`,
`enter`, `tab` and `escape`. For a sequence of chords, such as
`mod+k mod+s`, it uses only the first.

AppKit matches a key equivalent against the character the key types, so
Shift is written into the key and not into the mask: `mod+shift+o` is
`O` with Command, and `mod+shift+/` is `?` with Command, the character
Shift gives on a US keyboard. A named key such as an arrow types no
character, so it keeps the Shift bit.
[`mac_key`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#mac_key)
returns `None` for `hyper`, which a window manager takes, and for a
chord AppKit cannot show as a key equivalent, such as one with a
function key or an unknown modifier like `meta`.

``` python
mac_key('mod+p'), mac_key('mod+f5'), mac_key('meta+p')
```

    (('p', 1048576), None, None)

``` python
test_eq(mac_key('mod+P'), mac_key('mod+shift+p'))
test_eq(mac_key('mod+shift+o'), ('O', CMD))
test_eq(mac_key('mod+shift+/'), ('?', CMD))
test_eq(mac_key('mod+k mod+s'), mac_key('mod+k'))
```

### menu_chord

``` python
def menu_chord(
    action, lookup
):
```

*The AppKit chord for `action`: its first chord with a modifier, not
reserved, from a global binding or the only scope with that chord.*

A menu shortcut takes the key press before the web page sees it, so only
some of the host’s bindings should become one. The host’s keymap is
reached through `lookup`, a function that takes an action name and
returns a
[`Binding`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#binding)
from `kavacha.menus`, or `None`.
[`menu_chord`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#menu_chord)
looks up `action` and returns the AppKit chord of the binding’s first
chord that uses a modifier other than shift and is not in `RESERVED`,
and only when the binding either applies everywhere (its scope is
`global`) or is the only binding of that chord in any scope (`shared` is
false). A bare key such as `/`, or an editor chord that another pane
uses too, stays with the page. A lookup that returns some other object
with no `shared` attribute gets chords for its global bindings only.

``` python
KEYS = {'save':         Binding(('mod+s',), 'Save'),
        'quick_open':   Binding(('mod+shift+o',)),
        'find_in_file': Binding(('mod+f',), 'Find', scope='editor', shared=True),
        'cell_delete':  Binding(('mod+alt+backspace',), scope='editor'),
        'comment':      Binding(('/',), 'Comment'),
        'quit':         Binding(('mod+q',)),
        'orphan':       Binding()}
{a: menu_chord(a, KEYS.get) for a in KEYS}
```

    {'save': ('s', 1048576),
     'quick_open': ('O', 1048576),
     'find_in_file': None,
     'cell_delete': ('\x08', 1572864),
     'comment': None,
     'quit': None,
     'orphan': None}

`save` and `quick_open` are bound, global and use a modifier, so both
get their chord, and `quick_open` has Shift written into its key.
`find_in_file` applies only in the editor and another scope binds its
chord, so it stays with the page. `cell_delete` is scoped too, but no
other scope binds its chord, so it gets one. `comment` has no modifier,
`quit` is reserved and `orphan` has no key, so each of them gets `None`,
as does an action the keymap does not know.

A row’s label is the keymap’s `label`. When there is none,
[`_title`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#_title)
uses the action name with its underscores replaced by spaces and the
first letter capitalised, so a row is never blank and never shows a raw
identifier.

``` python
_title(MenuItem('save'), KEYS.get), _title(MenuItem('quick_open'), KEYS.get)
```

    ('Save', 'Quick open')

### menu_bar

``` python
def menu_bar(
    bar, lookup, on_action, run:NoneType=None
):
```

*Build pywebview menus from `bar`, and the row table
[`_decorate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#_decorate)
uses to add native shortcuts and selectors.*

[`menu_bar`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#menu_bar)
turns the host’s menu table into pywebview menus. `bar` is a list of
`(title, rows)` pairs, one per menu, and each row is one of the classes
in `kavacha.menus`. A
[`MenuItem`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#menuitem)
calls `on_action` with its action name, and a
[`MenuItem`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#menuitem)
without an action is a separator. A
[`Std`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#std) row is
handled by AppKit, and a
[`Js`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#js) row runs a
JavaScript expression in the focused window through
[`run`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/build.html#run), which is
[`eval_js`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#eval_js)
by default.
[`eval_js`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#eval_js)
returns what the expression evaluated to, or `None`.

pywebview cannot set a shortcut or an AppKit selector on a menu item, so
[`menu_bar`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#menu_bar)
also returns a table that maps `(menu title, row title)` to the row.
[`_decorate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#_decorate),
below, uses it to add those natively.

### install_menu_patch

``` python
def install_menu_patch(
    specs, lookup
):
```

*Reapply AppKit decoration whenever pywebview rebuilds the menu.*

pywebview rebuilds the native menu bar at times of its own choosing, and
each rebuild would lose those additions.
[`install_menu_patch`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#install_menu_patch)
wraps pywebview’s menu-building method so that
[`_decorate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#_decorate)
runs after every rebuild, and
[`exact_bar`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#exact_bar)
then moves the rows into a bar that matches chords exactly. It installs
the wrapper once per process and returns whether it did so on this call.

### exact_bar

``` python
def exact_bar(
    main
):
```

*A menu bar holding the rows of
[`main`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/lock.html#main), where a
row fires only for its own chord.*

AppKit lets a row with no Shift take the shifted chord of a key that has
no case: a row on ⌥↩ also runs for ⌥⇧↩, before the row that has ⌥⇧↩ gets
it.
[`exact_bar`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#exact_bar)
moves the rows into a bar that, for a Shift chord on such a key, first
runs the row whose chord is exactly the one pressed. Other chords go to
AppKit as before. The test builds both rows on a bar and presses each
chord.

[`_decorate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#_decorate)
walks the native menu bar and finishes each row it has a spec for. A
[`Std`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#std) row loses
its target and gets its AppKit selector, so the action goes to whatever
has focus, along with the row’s own chord. An action row gets the chord
[`menu_chord`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#menu_chord)
allows, if any. The menu titled `Window` becomes the app’s Windows menu,
where macOS lists the open windows.

### The menu bar as data

A launcher that builds its own native menu, in another language, needs
the same table with every chord already resolved.
[`menu_json`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#menu_json)
gives it: one `{'title', 'items'}` per menu, where an item is a
separator, an action row, a
[`Std`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#std) row with
its selector, or a
[`Js`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#js) row with its
expression.

On a Mac, a row carries `key` and `mask` when it has a chord. The chords
come from
[`menu_chord`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#menu_chord)
and
[`mac_key`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#mac_key),
the same as
[`_decorate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#_decorate)
uses.

Off a Mac (`mac=False`, for example a GTK launcher on Linux), a row
carries `chord`, the label to show, such as `Ctrl+Shift+P`. A row has
`accel`, a GTK accelerator, only when the launcher may bind it natively.
Those rows are the `PC_NATIVE` launcher rows (Quit, Close Window and
Full Screen) and the actions in `native`, such as a new window, which
the page never needs. Every other chord is a label only, so the key
press still reaches the page: Ctrl+C in a terminal is still an
interrupt.
[`pc_key`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#pc_key)
gives the [`Std`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#std)
chords, and
[`pc_menu_chord`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#pc_menu_chord)
picks an action’s chord as
[`menu_chord`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/window.html#menu_chord)
does, but it refuses the chords in
[`pc_reserved`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#pc_reserved).
A row that
[`pc_key`](https://vedicreader.github.io/kavacha/menus.html#pc_key)
removes is left out, and so is a separator with nothing to separate.
`mac=None` uses the platform the code runs on.
